A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Fréchet Wavelet Distance work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v2 reports original generator evaluations, retrained-Inception comparisons, sample-reweighting experiments and corruption tests in Tables 1–3 and Figure 6.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluations and adds computational measurements, Sentinel results and an original 50-volunteer perception study. The externally sourced ratings in Table 7 are distinct from these original results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same Haar wavelet-packet decomposition, pixel normalization, per-packet means and covariances, Fréchet distances and averaging procedure. The resolution-dependent transformation-depth rule is also retained. New evaluated generators and comparison metrics do not alter FWD.

E1.justification: v3 adds Sentinel remote-sensing imagery and Conceptual Captions text-to-image evaluation, while removing CIFAR-10 coverage entirely. It also adds human realism judgments. The DNDD description changes from sugar beet to winter wheat and rye, but retained sample counts and scores leave unclear whether this corrects documentation or reflects different underlying data.

E2.justification: FD-DINOv2 becomes a central evaluated comparator. Tables 8–9 add FID-infinity, IS, IS-infinity, Clean-FID and SWD, and introduce KID into the domain-bias comparison. PSNR and SSIM disappear, while FD-DINOv2 replaces KID in the reweighting and corruption comparisons. Some cross-domain retrained-Inception comparisons from v2 Table 2 are removed.

E3.justification: New protocols include real-versus-generated image choices with over 1,000 responses from 50 volunteers, Conceptual Captions evaluation against external user ratings, and feature-extraction GFLOPs and throughput measurements over 50,000 images. The reported Proj. FastGAN learning rate on CelebA-HQ and DNDD changes from 2e-4 to 1e-4; the PDFs do not establish whether those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds human-perception validation, an SWD-versus-FWD reproducibility analysis in Table 9, and a CelebA-HQ class-histogram comparison for DDGAN and Proj. FastGAN in Figure 5a. It extends the existing corruption and FID-optimization analyses to FD-DINOv2. The packet-interpretability analysis is retained, while some cross-domain retrained-backbone checks disappear.

E5.justification: Table 9 newly reports minimum, mean and standard deviation across five independent metric computations. Conversely, the retained reweighting results lose v2 Table 3's explicit five-run caption in v3 Table 6, although their uncertainty values remain. This does not establish a change in the underlying run count.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial numerical evidence for FD-DINOv2, Sentinel, EDM, human perception, efficiency and additional metrics. Existing ImageNet values also change: Improved Diffusion VLB has FID 42.257 and FWD 2.221 in v2 Table 1, versus 33.522 and 2.182 in v3 Table 4. With unchanged reweighting means, the reported FID change is corrected from -47% to -52.53%, and FWD from +2.5% to +17.75%. CIFAR-10 and several comparison entries are removed.

T1.justification: Equations 1–9 retain the same wavelet construction, statistical definitions and Fréchet-distance formulation. The appendix explanation of forward and inverse wavelet transforms is preserved. No substantive mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The original domain-agnostic, interpretable FWD contribution remains. v3 adds computational efficiency and FD-DINOv2's residual domain bias and high computational cost as explicit introduction contributions. The abstract and conclusion extend the critique to FD-DINOv2, and the conclusion adds environmental-cost and complementary-use claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations involving DINOv2 training-data overlap, SWD random-projection variability and StableDiffusion-2.1 image artifacts. It removes v2's explicit limitations concerning FWD's limited added utility on ImageNet, its frequency/spatial rather than semantic emphasis, and possible joint optimization of FWD and FID. These qualifications are not relocated to an appendix.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an explicit FWD implementation link and identifies the FD-DINOv2 code source. It documents the Sentinel winter subset, its 31,825 images, format conversion and generator-training settings, and identifies the StableDiffusion versions evaluated. Appendix compute information changes from A40 GPUs to A100 GPUs and ties the resources to sample generation. These materially expand or revise reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The positioning expands beyond Inception-based and traditional pairwise metrics to address FD-DINOv2 and SWD as important alternatives. New discussion cites Stein et al., Oquab et al. and Nguyen et al. to motivate training-domain, computational and reproducibility concerns. Additional generator and dataset references support the expanded evaluation; moving the spectral-method discussion to Appendix B is separately a structural change.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: domain bias leads, the broad generator comparison moves later, and a user-study section is introduced. Related-work material moves into Appendix B, appendices are reorganized into A–C, and the limitations section disappears. The introduction, results interpretation and conclusion are extensively revised, alongside language and author-information edits.

P2.justification: v3 restructures the benchmark and retrained-backbone tables, adds efficiency, perception and additional-metric tables, and introduces extensive sample grids in Appendix C. The corruption plot moves to the appendix with a changed comparator legend; the DNDD histogram moves into a combined main-text figure. Sample panels, captions, figure placement and the conference-template layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the empirical grounding of the unchanged metric through relevant FD-DINOv2 and other comparisons, measured computational cost, broader domains and an original human-realism study. These address important gaps in v2's perceptual validation and practical comparison. The implementation link and corrected percentages also help. Removing explicit limitations weakens balance, and Table 7 uses external ratings whose comparability to the evaluated samples is undocumented. Nevertheless, the direct comparisons and original human evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
